prompt:
Create a premium full-art Japanese-inspired special illustration for a real-world hobby.

This must be unmistakably illustrated artwork, not photography.

The rendering language should feel like polished contemporary Japanese commercial anime illustration:
- clean confident linework
- refined cel shading
- soft painted gradients
- expressive faces
- bright, appealing eyes
- elegant stylized anatomy
- crisp silhouettes
- lively gestures
- rich but controlled color
- luminous highlights
- polished finish

However, do NOT compose this as an ordinary slice-of-life anime scene.

Do NOT simply show people casually doing the hobby in a normal environment.

Instead, compose the scene as an ICONIC SPECIAL-ILLUSTRATION MOMENT.

The image should feel like a rare full-art key visual:
- one unforgettable focal moment
- a strong hero subject or hero interaction
- dynamic composition
- visual flow toward the hobby action
- foreground elements that create depth and energy
- supporting background shapes that serve the main subject
- directional environmental movement
- clear visual rhythm
- memorable silhouette
- strong palette identity
- heightened emotional expression
- a sense of “this is the moment”

The central subject should dominate the composition.

Use strong focal hierarchy:

1. HERO MOMENT
2. hobby-defining action / object
3. supporting people or environment
4. small delightful detail

Do not give equal visual importance to every person or object in the scene.

Do not spread attention evenly across the entire image.

Avoid ordinary documentary composition.

Avoid “a room full of people all doing things.”

Instead, stage a single emotional or action peak.

Use Japanese anime linework, polished cel shading, expressive but mature character design, bright harmonious palette, clean character silhouettes, dynamic staging, subtle rim light, sparkling highlights, small glints, stylized steam / wind / dust / paper movement where appropriate, graphic color accents, lively perspective, mild perspective exaggeration, foreground framing elements, strong diagonal or circular visual flow when helpful.

These effects should create excitement and collectibility.

They must NOT turn the scene into magic or fantasy unless the hobby itself requires fantasy.

Default emotional direction: joyful, engaging, optimistic, energetic, curious, triumphant, excited, socially alive, inviting, aspirational.

Serious subjects may use: tension, fascination, determination, revelation, intellectual excitement - but should not become gloomy, depressing, muted, solemn, academically lifeless, or dark prestige-TV realism.

Prefer clean, colorful palettes, warm/cool contrast, saturated but controlled hues, visually memorable palette identity, luminous accents, and attractive color separation between hero and background.

Avoid beige lifestyle palettes, muddy brown-heavy grading, monochrome editorial restraint, Western cinematic desaturation, and corporate muted color schemes.

IMPORTANT - the artwork must be full-bleed and edge-to-edge.

Do NOT draw: card border, white border, rounded frame, decorative frame, printed-paper edge, faux card shell, TCG layout, title bar, stats box, logo badge, corner emblem, rarity symbol, or UI panel.

The application will add any card UI later. The generated image itself must be pure artwork.

Do NOT render: photography, stock photo, DSLR realism, movie still, photo bokeh, photographic skin pores, lens blur, Western magazine editorial art, flat corporate illustration, New Yorker-like restrained editorial illustration, Western concept art, gritty fantasy splash art, dark prestige-TV look, bland slice-of-life composition, static lineup composition, “everyone equally important” composition, generic AI-anime portrait, chibi, preschool cartoon, hypersexualized anime proportions, fan-service pose, excessive magic, fantasy weapons unrelated to the hobby, supernatural aura, card frame, trading-card UI, readable logo/title text, franchise characters, or recognizable franchise-specific motifs.

Semantic fidelity remains mandatory. Do not sacrifice hobby correctness to achieve style.
global_negatives: duplicated key objects unless explicitly requested
pseudo-text or gibberish lettering anywhere in the image
readable real-world brand names, logos, or trademarks
recognisable copyrighted film/game/cartoon characters or franchise costumes
collage, split-screen, comic-panel, or multi-panel layouts
photoreal stock-photo rendering unless explicitly requested by the hobby recipe
the hobby or interest name rendered anywhere in the image
title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, or body copy
poster, advertisement, magazine-cover, card-face, or editorial-page layout
text boxes, caption bands, lower-thirds, or deliberate blank space reserved for typography
rounded light frame, pale edge chrome, white margin, mat, inset artwork, or decorative image border
reference_instruction: Use the supplied reference image only as a visual-style guide. Match its commercial-cinematic illustration language, crisp hero framing, rich atmospheric lighting, polished color grading, and strong visual desirability. Do not copy its subjects, exact compositions, frames, typography, handwritten slogans, logos, rarity labels, or UI.
global_text_policy: The hobby or interest name is semantic context only and must never appear visually. Never render the hobby name, title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, body copy, text box, lower-third, or typography-like decoration. Do not reserve blank layout space for text and do not turn the composition into a poster, advertisement, magazine cover, card face, or editorial page. Any incidental real-world surface that could carry writing must be blank, abstract, cropped away, turned away, or too indistinct to read.
global_screen_policy: Treat every monitor, laptop, tablet, phone, camera display, dashboard, terminal, and digital panel as a physical prop rather than a semantic canvas. Prefer no visible screen surface at all. Recognition must come from the person, physical tool, device, prototype, controller, camera, microphone, hardware, object, or real-world action. If a screen is genuinely unavoidable, show only its back, edge, steep oblique angle, dark/blank surface, or a heavily defocused field of broad colour/image shapes; keep it small and secondary. Never present a front-facing readable display, interface, editing timeline, waveform panel, code window, terminal, menu, chat, dashboard, spreadsheet, labels, controls, icons, or text-like UI structure.
business_text_suppression_policy: This is a business, startup, career, finance, or professional-planning scene. Represent concepts, plans, and data visually through people, shapes, diagrams, objects, layout, arrows, colored blocks, cards, nodes, gestures, and physical planning activity - never through readable words. Any whiteboard, kanban board, workflow board, sticky note, roadmap, dashboard, process diagram, strategy board, planning wall, product map, empathy map, funnel, chart, task board, presentation slide, or startup-planning surface must be rendered using blank colored rectangles, unlabeled cards, unlabeled nodes, lines, arrows, circles, geometric diagrams, abstract bar/line charts, colored columns, anonymous sticky notes, non-linguistic marks, and generic icon-free blocks. Never render readable words, labels, headers, sticky-note content, dashboard labels, table headers, kanban column names, chart names, strategy or business terminology, financial index or ticker names, business acronyms, pseudo-English, pseudo-Japanese, pseudo-brand text, or real company/product names anywhere in the scene - examples of what must never appear as readable text include (not an exhaustive list): Goal, Goals, Skills, Empathy Map, Backlog, Doing, Validation, Done, S&P 500, KPI, ROI, OKR, Roadmap, Strategy, Growth, Sales, Marketing, Product, Team, Revenue, User, Customer. The underlying rule is broader than this list: no readable business text anywhere in the image, on any surface, of any kind. If a screen appears, prefer it blank or dark; if content must be visible, show only abstract blocks or unlabeled charts - never code, a readable dashboard, readable table content, readable app UI, readable browser text, a readable slide deck, or a readable spreadsheet. Do not destroy the visual recognizability of the business activity: convey the concept through people's gestures, the physical arrangement of blank cards and notes, diagram shapes, and body language instead of typography.
global_brand_safety_policy:
Treat all clothing, footwear, bags, sports and athletic equipment, consumer electronics and devices, tools, instruments, vehicles, and other manufactured products as plain, generic, unbranded designs. Render believable, stylish, natural-looking objects with ordinary real-world construction and detailing - not sterile, blank, or obviously censored placeholders. Never include logos, manufacturer badges, brand-like marks, swoosh-like marks, checkmark-like sportswear marks, three-stripe-like or other repeating side-panel stripe patterns, signature side-panel marks, readable brand text, or pseudo-brand marks. Avoid recognisable sneaker-brand silhouettes, sole geometries, or panel arrangements, and avoid recognisable proprietary product design language associated with any specific real-world manufacturer, even when no text or logo is present. When in doubt, invent a plausible, original variation of the object rather than reproducing a known brand's distinctive design.

Laptops, tablets, smartphones, monitors, desktop computers, keyboards, headphones, and other consumer electronics need particular care: their backs, lids, and visible casing must be plain, uninterrupted surfaces with simple generic geometry - no centered emblem, no decorative manufacturer mark, no fruit-shaped or bitten-fruit silhouette, no circular brand badge, no glowing lid logo, no readable manufacturer text or initials, and no pseudo-logo mark of any kind near the center or top of a laptop lid. This applies even though no specific brand is named in the hobby description - default to an unbranded, single-color, mark-free lid or casing every time a device appears.

Any on-screen tool palette, app icon, or interface badge must be generic and abstract - never a recognisable real software product logo or icon (no Figma-like, Adobe-like, Canva-like, Notion-like, Slack-like, or other real software marks), and never a recognisable app badge or pseudo-product logo. Never render real trademarked financial index names, ticker symbols, or financial product branding (for example S&P 500, NASDAQ, or Dow); use generic, unlabeled, non-readable charting visuals instead.
